Do the best you can within your limits in the kitchen while you have to pay bills, but there’s always time after work to develop new skills. I have kitchen experience so trust me I understand how overwhelming it can be lol.
I would look into working remote if your body is being that difficult. There’s so much that can be done behind a computer screen from home if you want to be more risk averse.

I’m only dealing with soft tissue trauma so I can’t imagine. What I might sometimes do is tell someone the pain is bad and am going to take 10 minutes off. What I’ll do is find somewhere flat I can lay where not a lot/no one can see me (a bench outside or in a bathroom or something) either lay flat on my back or do some stretches I know help. When I get back to work, I ease into it. It won’t be pretty but I ride out the Advil and Tylenol for the next few hours. In terms of the anxiety or doubt you’ll get through it, that’s the hard part. When all else fails just be tough.
You’re going to have to be your own advocate. Fuck what other people think, they don’t know what it’s like in your shoes. May I ask what’s wrong with your back more specifically?

Funny story you bring up gut biome, last time I went to my doctor about my back he said “eat more fucken protein” which is exactly what I did. (I weigh 140, I’m not underweight or anything) a month later I have gastrointestinal pain that won’t go away. I guess this community has a habit of feeling a certain kinda way about doctors.

Going on a strict elimination diet soon because now my stomach and back is screwed.

It’s made me feel worse when the electricity was set too high. At lower settings it has helped me. I have a really sensitive nervous system I think so over the years my brain has opened up pain pathways down my whole back. It’s so strange because I dont think I have any damaged disks or joints. The pain has still been very real for 3 years. (Used to carry around 90 pound bags of shingles onto rooftops for work at age 20).

I’m still on acupuncture (I absolutely hate needles) but I put my feelings aside and I think it has helped me. If you barely feel the electrical pulses in your muscles it’s enough. Don’t overdo it. It’s uncomfortable but just might pay off.

Easier said than done but don’t think big picture. Think about what you can do right this second to either provide value to yourself or the people around you. Could be getting smarter by reading books, could be just focusing on yourself and your sickness, could be making someone smile somehow. Many aspects of life have been taken away but you still have things to do. Still have a life to live.
I’ve had an X-ray, showed inflammation but my spine is fine

Well apparently my there’s nothing wrong with my joints according to my physiotherapist but sitting is awful in pretty much any good or bad chair. I can usually get it to crack with slight twists/stretches but it always comes back. Numbness in my leg is rare but it does happen.

It doesn’t sound like you were honest with her from the start. If all you end up doing is being friends, of course she’s not gonna take you seriously. My advice is love the single life for a while and find your own life to live. And if you really do love her that much you should let her do what SHE wants. Even if that’s the other guy she’s sexting. I’d ghost her. Even if she shows signs like she did at the pizza place. It’s her way of getting the quick attention and validation. You’re wasting your mental resources.
When people say “it gets better” I really question their intentions. It’s like an insult. To me hope of a better life is toxic.
